corpusSummary: Corpus presents a multi-disciplinary snapshot of 2026 studies on large language models, emphasizing human–AI interaction, AI as a research tool, AI-enhanced education, and health/public-policy implications. Across settings from health misinformation to classroom scaffolding and public governance, papers probe trust, ethics, equity, bias, interpretability, and the sustainability of AI deployments, while exploring design of safer, more transparent, and socially aware AI systems.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, governance, and social impact
themes.description: A cross-cutting thread examining user trust, adoption barriers, ethical considerations, equity, embodiment, and mis/disinformation in AI-enabled decision making.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological governance in social science
themes.description: Papers explore how LLMs support coding, content analysis, simulations, and data-driven insights, while highlighting validation, transparency, reproducibility, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Studies assess AI-enabled tutoring, scaffolding, classroom integration, and AI literacy interventions across learners from K-12 to older adults.

themes.name: Health, misinformation, and public health communication in AI contexts
themes.description: A cluster focusing on AI-generated health information, misinformation sharing, patient education, and AI-assisted clinical reasoning and decision support.
